newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA START TOUR WITH CRUSHING WIN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA START TOUR WITH CRUSHING WIN.

text.p: Australia gave the first hint of what England can expect in the forthcoming Ashes series with a comprehensive 113-run victory over the Duke of Norfolk's XI on Thursday.

The invitation side crumbled to 122 all out in cool, overcast conditions as Jason Gillespie and Michael Kasprowicz took the opportunity to show that Australia's bowling threat is not simply confined to Shane Warne and Glenn McGrath.

Gillespie took four for 21 in six impressive overs and Kasprowicz three for 17, reducing the home team to 59 for eight until a ninth-wicket stand of 60 between 44-year-old John Emburey and Neal Radford prolonged the contest.

The touring side will also have been encouraged by the initial efforts of captain Mark Taylor and his former test opening partner Michael Slater, both influential members of the 1993 Ashes side seeking to revive their test careers.

Taylor, who has given himself a month to find some form after going 20 test innings without a fifty, was not at his most fluent but still made 45 off 86 balls, with five fours, before being outwitted by ex-England off-spinner Emburey.

Slater, seeking to regain his place as an opener, did his best to catch the eye down the order, hoisting three sixes and cracking the final delivery of the innings for four to reach a 53-ball half-century.
Most of the other Australian batsmen also stayed at the crease long enough to give themselves a feel of English conditions, with Mark Waugh looking in supreme touch in making 46 from 53 balls.

Emburey, captaining an assorted team of ex-test players, unsung county pros and Zimbabwe's Flower brothers, held things in check with a miserly 10-over spell of two for 25, but the Australian total of 235 for five was never remotely under pressure.

Arundel remains an English cricket ground straight out of central casting with its chestnut trees, striped marquees and perfect billiard-table outfield, but the host side's batting effort scarcely did the setting justice.
Ignoring light drizzle, Kasprowicz took three of the first four wickets to fall and Gillespie ensured an early finish.
Australia's next game is against Northamptonshire on Saturday, the first of three limited-over contests against county sides before the international one-day series starts next Thursday.
